title: ESG investments: Filtering versus machine learning approaches

extraction.methodology_summary: The authors design a supervised machine learning algorithm that maps granular ESG indicators into regions (hyper-rectangles defined by If-Then rules) predicting 3-month forward excess returns. The rule predictions are aggregated through convex combination and transformed into discrete scores of {-1, 0, +1}. Simple long-only portfolios are formed by screening for stocks with positive scores (+1) and compared against traditional ESG best-in-class exclusion portfolios.
extraction.data_period: January 2013 to March 2018 (algorithm trained starting from 2009)
extraction.universe: MSCI World Index (large-cap equities across US, Canada, Western Europe, Japan, Australia, New Zealand, Hong Kong, and Singapore)
key_findings: Simple ESG best-in-class filtering approaches do not generate significant outperformance or alpha over broad universes like the MSCI World Index.
Granular ESG indicators contain valuable predictive signals that can be successfully extracted using non-linear machine learning techniques.
The Positive ML Screening strategy significantly outperforms both the benchmark and standard ESG best-in-class portfolios.
Regularly updating and retraining the machine learning algorithm over time is crucial because the predictive power of the rules vanishes over time.
limitations: The out-of-sample testing period is relatively short, covering five years and three months from January 2013 to March 2018.
